title: P2 inheritance for the extended permutation construction
summary: Decide whether the source's one-bit extension of a permutation always preserves the P2 second-derivative property when the input permutation has P2.

formal_statement.body: Let $\sigma:\mathbb F_2^m\to\mathbb F_2^m$ be a permutation satisfying the source-defined property (P2), and define $\pi(y,t)=(y+t(\sigma(y)+y),t)$ on $\mathbb F_2^m\times\mathbb F_2$. Must $\pi$ satisfy the full (P2) property for every admissible $m$ and $\sigma$? Prove the inheritance theorem or give a counterexample.

scope.domain: Permutations used in bent-function constructions and their P2 derivative property
assumptions: sigma is a permutation of F_2^m
sigma satisfies the source-defined P2 property
pi is the construction in Equation (IV.1)
scope.unresolved_remainder: A later theorem proves P2 for this construction under the stronger premise that id+sigma has P2. Whether sigma having P2 alone suffices, or admits a counterexample, remains open.

progress.summary: The source leaves universal P2 inheritance for its Equation (IV.1) construction open.
A later theorem proves inheritance for the strict subfamily in which id+sigma, rather than sigma alone, satisfies P2.
